correctness.rationale: Exact IID-priority model: pair indicator equals the event that the minimum priority of its rank interval is at an endpoint. Disjoint and strict-nested joint probabilities are 4/(uv); shared-endpoint, touching, and interleaving cases give respectively (s+2)/(s*l), (1+2/u+2/v)/(u+v-1), and (2/t)(1/u+1/v). Subtracting 4/(uv) yields each stated sign and boundary. For mutual independence, removal of a minimal interval reveals its argmin identity is independent of its minimum value and all external priorities, and the other indicators depend on the removed interval only through its minimum. Induct. Conversely every forbidden nontrivial pair has nonzero covariance. The finite checker passed 935 exact-rational assertions including 11 strict-laminar triple events at sizes <=8; these are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The full comparison-event dependence structure of a fundamental randomized sorting algorithm is a natural question beyond total expected cost. The all-size signed covariance kernel identifies which interactions repel, attract, or vanish. The necessary-and-sufficient characterization proves exact joint independence for arbitrary-size strict-laminar families, enabling rigorous product probabilities and weighted-count computations unavailable from the classical marginal or total-variance facts. This is a structural probability theorem, not an arbitrary finite sample or minor numeric improvement.
